violation: magelib has zero test files. `find . -name '*_test.go'` returns 0 across the repo, so `mage test` reports `[no test files]` and exits 0: a green gate that tests nothing, the same shape as GAPI-DIV-042's empty fuzz corpus. This is the library implementing Lint, Doctor, CheckHermetic, BufGenerate and Release for the entire ecosystem, so every gate in gapi and goblin is enforced by untested code, and MAGELIB-DIV-002 is a direct consequence: a defect in the schema treaty's baseline selection survived because nothing exercised it. BufGenerate's baseline selection is extracted as `breakingPlan(against) (baseline, skip)`, so the decision is testable without `buf`, including PROTO_BREAKING_SKIP taking precedence over PROTO_BREAKING_AGAINST (a0f10a7). Lint's carve-out plumbing is extracted as `gosecArgs(excludes)` and asserted to emit one joined `-exclude=` flag, because gosec takes the last one it is given, alongside `SharedLintConfig`'s local-over-sibling precedence (8d59b7c). CI exists and runs it: .github/workflows/ci.yml, jobs `Build and Test` and `Ecosystem Gates`, required by an org ruleset, and run 30656525451 on this branch showed a non-zero test count. `mage test` now passes -v, which is load-bearing rather than noise: without it the only output is the package summary line, which a fully-skipped package prints identically to a fully-passing one, so the run log could not evidence a count at all. This entry's own standard is a gate demonstrated by a failing run on an introduced defect, and a green-only history satisfies the first half of that and not the second - the same shape as MAGELIB-DIV-002 before its negative test, and as GAPI-DIV-042's empty corpus this entry cites. Closing requires a pull request that introduces a deliberate defect in pkg/magelib, the required `Build and Test` check going red on it, and the PR becoming unmergeable. WHAT THE GATE DOES NOT CATCH, recorded rather than solved: nothing asserts `mg.Deps(checkHermetic)` stays wired to Build, Test and Lint - deleting it is a silent regression, because the Magefile still compiles and every target still goes green. `Magefile.go` is //go:build mage and outside the package graph, so no test in pkg/magelib can reach it; this is the identical residual both sibling repos recorded for checkTerminology in GAPI-DIV-044 and GOBLIN-DIV-045. violation: The schema treaty could not fail in CI. BufGenerate ran `buf breaking` against whatever baseline its callers hardcoded, and both callers pass `.git#ref=HEAD` (gapi/Magefile.go:203, goblin/Magefile.go:189). That baseline is correct for a developer comparing an edited working tree against the last commit and inert anywhere the working tree IS the commit: on a fresh CI checkout buf compares the schema against itself. Demonstrated in goblin with `string method = 2` retyped to `int64` in proto/goblin/v1/rpc.proto: `buf breaking --against .git#ref=HEAD` on the dirty tree exits 100 with the field-level message, while `buf breaking --against .` on the identical tree exits 0. Any CI job wrapped around `mage proto` before this was fixed would have been green by construction, installing review-v2 finding 1's exact pathology into the mechanism the ecosystem manifesto names as the treaty between repos. GOBLIN-DIV-036 compounds it: the payloads buf would police are JSON, so even a correct baseline sees only the envelope.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto section 5 (buf breaking is the schema treaty between repos); go-project-manifesto (a gate that cannot fail is not a gate)

violation: The hermeticity guarantee stops exactly where the gate's real work begins. CheckHermetic verifies that `go`, `gcc` and `protoc` - plus `pandoc` when it is present on PATH - resolve under /nix/store, then checks the toolchain pin. It does not check `buf`, `golangci-lint` or `gosec`. Since 1430285 wired `mg.Deps(checkHermetic)` to Build, Test and Lint, Lint now guarantees a hermetic Go toolchain and then shells out to three tools none of which were checked: golangci-lint and gosec directly (lint.go), buf via BufGenerate (proto.go). Each of the three could come from anywhere on PATH, including a host install. A host golangci-lint of a different version silently changes what the lint gate enforces; a host buf silently changes the schema treaty MAGELIB-DIV-002 exists to keep honest. What makes this an entry rather than a footnote is the asymmetry: `DoctorConfig.SharedTools` exists precisely so a repo can extend the hermetic tool list, and this repo's own Magefile.go passes buf, golangci-lint, gosec, govulncheck, mage and goimports to Doctor, which feeds them to checkHermeticResolution. So the doctor checks these tools and the gate that depends on them does not - and the doctor is advisory, run when an operator asks, while Lint runs in CI on every push. CheckHermetic takes no parameter through which a caller could close the gap.
rule: build-environment.md (targets run through the pinned shell; hermetic resolution comes from the pinned store); go-project-manifesto (a gate that cannot fail is not a gate - one whose enforcing tools are unpinned reports a result it did not control)
exit: Closes on a GATE, not on a list. CheckHermetic must cover every tool the shared targets actually execute, so that a shell missing one - or a host copy sitting ahead of the store one on PATH - fails the target that needs the tool rather than the target after it. The tool set is data, not a constant: whatever carries it must be the same mechanism DoctorConfig.SharedTools already feeds, so the doctor and the gate cannot drift apart by construction, and it must stay per-repo, because gapi's plugin set is not goblin's. Demonstrated by a run that goes red with a host tool shadowing the store one, not by a commit that adds three names to `baseTools`. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS SILENTLY FALSE AGAIN, recorded rather than solved: the checked set is a list, and a target that begins shelling out to some new tool does not fail for having skipped it - it simply leaves the list quietly incomplete, which is this entry's own finding recurring one tool later. Nothing asserts the wiring either: per MAGELIB-DIV-001, Magefile.go is //go:build mage and unreachable from pkg/magelib tests, so removing the dep leaves every target green. And checkStorePath falls back to the unresolved PATH entry when filepath.EvalSymlinks returns an error, so a tool whose symlink cannot be read is judged on where it was found rather than on where it points, and a /nix/store-prefixed link to somewhere else passes.
